reason: The manuscript is an 18-word-short draft (582 words against the 600-word floor) built around a climate reparations frame that no source in the research packet actually supports. The primary source — the Grist/ICT News report on Indigenous delegates at EMRIP in Geneva — documents climate-conflict intersection and UNDRIP's troubled twentieth anniversary. It does not discuss climate reparations as a concept, demand, or policy debate. The writer model was forced to invent a reparations accountability frame to satisfy the assignment term, producing editorial conclusions that outrun every source in the packet and a section heading that mechanically stamps the SEO term onto material it does not fit. The deterministic word-count gate failure is the least serious problem here; the structural mismatch between assignment term and source content is the root cause.

The manuscript fails one deterministic gate — body-too-short, 377 words against a 600-word floor — and carries a structural editorial defect: no section connects the NextBSD revival to Koios's collapse frame. Every factual claim traces cleanly to the single admitted source. The headline and lede are faithful, attribution is preserved throughout, and no claims are invented. The piece is honest but too thin and off-frame for publication.

The piece has a sound evidential spine. Its central claims — the EMRIP 19th session in Geneva, the near-20-year gap since UNDRIP adoption, the compounding pressures of climate, conflict, and state action, and the Binota Moy Dhamai quote — are all traceable to the supplied ICT News source, and the Nepal section stays within the limits of what the Cultural Survival headline asserts. The deterministic gate correctly cleared this piece. It fails on prose grounds: the thesis is repeated almost verbatim three times, a single phrasing appears twice word-for-word, the SEO term is unnaturally bolted onto a section heading, original authorship of the primary source is not surfaced, and capitalization of "Indigenous" is inconsistent. These are bounded, repairable defects. No pipeline layer upstream of draft-repair needs to change.

The piece establishes a coherent, well-sourced introduction to the Fullbrook/Morgan collection in its first two sections. Attribution is clean, the headline and lede are faithful to the sources, and the specific claims about green growth policy instruments and the ecomodernist premise are all grounded in the van Woerden and RWER sources. The piece fails in the third section, which recycles points already made in sections one and two without advancing reader understanding and closes with confident rhetorical abstractions that substitute performance for information. A bounded repair to that section would make the piece publishable.

The manuscript makes a coherent analytical argument about Woodside Energy's industrial AI adoption as a case study in what "autonomous enterprise" actually requires, and it draws a legitimate secondary connection to vendor cost-shifting via the Forrester/Register source. The deterministic gate cleared and the structural underpinnings of the main argument are supportable. The piece fails on two bounded but material editorial grounds: it uses the weather data sabotage source in a way that the evidence doesn't justify, constructing an analogy the stories themselves do not draw and that only superficially illuminates the main thesis; and the manuscript's handling of the likely-branded-content nature of the primary MIT Technology Review source is inadequately hedged given how load-bearing that source is. Neither defect is fatal. The repairs are bounded and the underlying argument survives.

Both defects are bounded and correctable in the draft without replaying from the writer model.
